sections.heading: Fighting Against Magic
sections.markdown:
- Magic Fortification/Barrier of Gold, increases Magic damage negation by 35%/60% (10%/20% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user, lasting for 90 seconds/70 seconds. Barrier of Gold additionally grants the buff to nearby allies. Requires 10 and 24 Faith to cast.
- Protection of the Erdtree, increases Magic damage negation by 35% (10% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user and nearby allies for 70 seconds. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount. Requires 35 Faith to cast.
- Spelldrake Talisman/Spelldrake Talisman +1/Spelldrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Magic damage negation by 13%/17%/20% (4%/5%/6% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time.

- Spellproof Dried Liver, a consumable and Body Buff that increases Magic damage negation by 15% (10% in PvP). Lasts for 120 seconds.
- Pest's Glaive, a Halberd that increases Magic damage negation by 2%. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount. Only works if held in an active hand and does not stack with another Pest's Glaive.

Effect stacks if wearing several pieces at the same time (though the two Chest armor pieces cannot be worn at the same time) for a maximum damage increase of 8%.

Maps are a type of Key Item found in Elden Ring. They are found in fragmented pieces across the Lands Between, and each piece displays an artistic rendition of their local region's geography. Once a map fragment has been acquired, it will become a permanent addition to the player's inventory, staying even when transitioning into .

They are typically found near large, stone Guide Stele inscribed with glowing yellow text that fades once that tablet's map has been acquired. These tablets are typically found near roads and are even marked on the obscured map before the current region's map fragment has been acquired.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Royal Knight Loretta**, also known as **Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree**, is a recurring, optional Great Enemy boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Loretta is the boss of two locations: Caria Manor and Miquella's Haligtree. Her oath-sworn spectral form—Royal Knight Loretta—is found at the former, while her corporeal body defends the latter. Loretta is mechanically similar to the Tree Sentinels and Draconic Tree Sentinels and cannot be separated from her steed.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Loretta was once a royal Carian knight, and served as a personal guard for Carian royalty. Loretta's favored weapon was said to be the bow, and she developed sorceries imitating the power of a greatbow.

Loretta eventually became concerned with the plight of the Albinaurics and embarked on a long and bloody journey searching for a haven for the Albinauric people. She determined that the Haligtree was their best chance for eventual salvation. It was rumored she was actually an Albinauric herself, due to the shape and symbolism associated with her Silver Mirrorshield. She would eventually find it at the Haligtree, in service to demigod Miquella, where she now remains.

Loretta appears to have entered into Miquella's service, replacing the blue glintstone that once adorned her war sickle with unalloyed gold. Now she stands guard within the Haligtree, refusing to abandon her post although Miquella himself is long gone. Her lapis-lazuli blue cape is the emblem of the knightly pride that continues to guide her.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Royal Knight Loretta** is a boss in Elden Ring. She can be found at Caria Manor in the Royal Moongazing Grounds.

She appears to be an apparition of Loretta summoned to guard Caria Manor, just as the real Loretta presumably used to do before leaving her duty to help find sanctuary for the mistreated Albinaurics.

Defeating her disables the magical spell of warding that complicates the approach to the Manor.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree** is a mini-boss in Elden Ring found in Miquella's Haligtree and is required to progress to Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. This boss is a stronger version of Royal Knight Loretta, found in Caria Manor.

It is possible to parry Loretta's halberd swings.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Defeating Royal Knight Loretta for the first time unlocks the "Royal Knight Loretta" achievement. Similarly, defeating Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree for the first time unlocks the "Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree" achievement.
- Loretta is presumed to be an Albinauric Archer in disguise.
 - Rumored to be an Albinauric, she cares deeply for them, abandoning her duty to travel to the Haligtree.
 - This female character appears only on horseback and demonstrates unmatched skill with the bow.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
The **Land of Reeds** (葦の地, *Ashi no Chi*) is a mentioned location in Elden Ring.

It is located outside the borders of the Lands Between and is said to be a place locked in a long and miserable civil war, which, over time, has caused its alienation from neighboring nations and left the entire land succumbed to a blood-soaked madness.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Land of Reeds is home to a caste of warriors known as Samurai, who wield katanas designed to inflict blood loss. Cone-shaped hats woven from straw are also worn in the Land of Reeds.

The warrior, Okina, was a swordsman from the Land of Reeds. It is said that through repeated combat, his mind was sharpened. From his perspective, he began to see the absurdities of the world in stark relief. As a result, he chose to renounce everything, ascending to a plane where it only himself, his katana, and his mastery. Before long, Okina had become a demon of a swordsman. For unknown reasons; perhaps seeking stronger opponents, Okina travelled to the Lands Between. There, he met Mohg, Lord of Blood, in battle. Upon feeling OkIna's blade strike his flesh, Mohg realised the extent of the Reedlander's maddness, and was captivated. In that moment, he made the swordsman an offer: a life in which his thirst for blood would never be sated. Okina agreed, joining the ranks of Mohg's Bloody Fingers. In return, Mohg coated his katana in cursed blood, so that Okina could better pursue his bloodlust.

During Okina's time in the Land of Reeds, his talents had earned a loyal following of fellow warriors known as the Inaba, who became his disciples. The Inaba, and potentially Okina himself, practiced Seppuku, a forbidden combat technique developed in the Land of Reeds. It involves the user impaling themselves with their own weapon, briefly enchanting it to improve damage output and its abilty to inflict blood loss on others. Having been abandoned by Okina when he left for the Lands Between, the Inaba soon pursued their former master, seeking revenge and death in battle, as was their ultimate goal.

sections.heading: People
sections.markdown: The peoples hailing from this land are referred to as "Reedlanders" and are select-able as a base template for the player character's appearance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Its history, weapons and mentioned customs are extremely reminiscent of the Sengoku (warring states) period of Japan, during the the 15th and 16th centuries.
 - One of the legendary names of ancient Japan was 葦原の中つ国 (*Ashihara-no-Nakatsu-Kuni)*, which translates literally to "The Land Amongst the Reeds." (More idiomatically, it might be read "the land of abundant rice.")
- Although never directly stated, many details suggest the Land of Reeds is under the influence of the Formless Mother. These include descriptions of Reedlanders as having "succumbed to a blood-soaked madness" and their clear favoritism for weapons that cause Blood Loss. The Outer God delights in the inflicting of wounds and the spilling of blood in all forms. The magical enhancement granded by Seppuku may very well be a blessing from the Outer God, with the technique acting as a form of offering. If the Formless Mother does preside over the Land of Reeds, it remains unclear if Reedlanders are willing to serve it, or if they are even aware of it.

 - Unlike the other Liver items this item's cookbook is acquired far later in the game, making it unavailable for Leyndell, Royal Capital, one of the game's major Lightning-focused area.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Magnus the Beast Claw is an NPC that can be invaded. To invade him, one must go to the Writheblood Ruins and find an invading summon sign, which costs one Festering Bloody Finger each try to activate. Once the sign is activated, the player will invade Magnus' world with the objective of killing him. The main point of this NPC is to have another option to advance in White Mask Varré's questline, where the Tarnished is tasked to try invasions 3 times, of either him or other players (though defeating him also counts as all 3 invasions).

Though there are few, if any, hints as to his place in the world, under his mask his face has vertical red markings similar to those borne by the Ancestral Follower Warriors.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.markdown:
- Both Beast Claw and Gurranq's Beast Claw can be jumped over.
 - This means they serve as good openings for jumping attacks, should you be ready to approach as he starts them up.
- Bestial Sling can simply be dodged through straight forwards and he's unlikely to spam it, limiting its power.
- Having both a Great Hammer (one with Lion's Claw as its skill at that) makes it rather unsafe to block him, especially with anything that isn't at least a decent Greatshield.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Lanya** is a character in Elden Ring. She is a servant of House Hoslow and childhood companion of Diallos Hoslow.

Described by Diallos as being "fickle as the wind," she has a habit of running off to unknown places, frequently requiring him to search for her whereabouts.

She would eventually meet her fate in the middle of one of her disappearances, having been murdered by an unspecified Recusant of Volcano Manor, and her body was left in a pool of blood at the northern edge of Academy Gate Town. This act that would put Diallos on a path of revenge; however, true to his nature, he was unable to commit to the act in the end, instead joining the Recusants himself as a prospective champion. He would still feel pain and sadness over Lanya's death, calling it cruel and unfortunate, but believed they were both simply laid hard roads by fate.

sections.markdown:
Lanya has a slender figure and mild orange skin with faintly visible freckles covering her cheeks. Her eyes are light blue. She has messy, orange-blonde hair that reaches down to her shoulders, with some covering her left eye and some tied into a small ponytail at the top of her head.

She wears the Chain Armor, Chain Gauntlets and Chain Leggings.

However, she is nowhere near a cliff and has suffered a violent end, making it less likely (but not impossible) to have been Patches.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Lord of Frenzied Flame** (狂い火の王, *Kurui Hi no Ō*), also known as the **Lord of Chaos** (混沌の王, *Konton no Ō*), is a status and title in the world of Elden Ring. It refers to the prophesied, messiah-like figure of the Frenzied Flame and its ailing followers. Promising them salvation from their torment, despair, their affliction, every sin, and every curse by melting it all away.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A chosen few of those afflicted with the flame of frenzy are capable of transforming into the Lord after an apparent death, or a process of rebirth, it's not clear and it's left to speculation. The strength of its form can seemingly vary depending on its original host, with several having proven capable of becoming one. However, many of them were either too weak-willed or physically feeble to accomplish anything, causing them to be considered frauds and failures in the eyes of their followers.

Similar to the power of its namesake, it has an uncanny ability to erase the original identity of its vessel. However, in the case of the Tarnished, it's unclear whether his identity is truly erased. Given his ability to subdue demigods and gods like the Elden Beast, it is plausible that he did not succumb to the Flame, but instead mastered it—fusing with it rather than being consumed. It can apparently emerge from its host even if they don't want it to and could even prompt them to abruptly die at a moment's notice to force their transformation into itself. Either way, the constraints of the transformation are left open to interpretation within the lore.

Once a Lord of Frenzied Flame manifests, the head of the original host is replaced by a black hole with yellow flames spewing out of its core, apparently erasing any visible trace of the original host's identity. In the case of Midra, it moves his body around with mannerisms completely alien to not only the original host but even other chaos followers as well. Making gestures that suggest complete delight and overwhelming euphoria at the sight of its flames consuming everything in its path. An ironic contrast for something supposedly being born from unspeakable torment and despair. However, since Midra is regarded as a failed Lord, that might not fully apply to the Tarnished, or it may manifest differently—yet still in a similar way to Midra or other candidates, should they possess a stronger will.

While it is seen as a savior from the perspective of those stricken by madness, it is a harbinger of insanity and death to everyone else. A menace to all life and the joys of living.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Lord of Frenzied Flame** is one of the possible endings in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending is the legacy of Shabriri, Finger Maiden Hyetta, and the Three Fingers. As the Lord of Frenzied Flame, the player shall burn away all that divides and distinguishes, allowing chaos to take the world.
Warning**: Progressing the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending locks the player out of other endings and causes Melina to cut ties with the player, vowing to kill them. The player can change to a different ending by inserting Miquella's Needle at storm beyond time; however, this action cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.markdown:
The "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending is achieved by inheriting the Frenzied Flame from the Three Fingers at the Frenzied Flame Proscription and finishing the game at Fractured Marika without using Miquella's Needle at Crumbling Farum Azula.

The smoldering stone door at the Frenzied Flame Proscription can be opened after the player unequips all Armor. Opening it initiates a cutscene in which the Three Fingers bestow the power of Frenzied Flame. Interacting with the Three Fingers causes Melina to leave permanently, vowing to kill the player Tarnished. However, the player can bypass her sacrifice by using the Fingers' flame as kindling to awaken the Flame of Ruin at the Forge of the Giants and commit the Cardinal Sin. The player can still meet the Three Fingers if they have already used Melina to burn the Erdtree. The Three Fingers do not clasp the player again if they cheat fate by inserting Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time.

If her questline has been advanced, Finger Maiden Hyetta will wait patiently on the side of the hall opposite the Site of Grace. She urges the Tarnished to seek an audience with the Three Fingers, whose sanctum lies beyond a large stone door that was partially melted by searing fingerprints. The door may only be opened once and only after unequipping all armor. After receiving the Flame of Frenzy, speak with Hyetta, who can then interpret the words of the Fingers to their chosen Lord of Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The "Lord of the Frenzied Flame" ending will unlock the Lord of Frenzied Flame achievement.
- Meeting Lightseeker Hyetta and completing her questline are optional steps for getting the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending. Her questline can still be started after interacting with the Three Fingers, though it proceeds as if the player has not yet received the Frenzied Flame. Choosing to "**Touch Hyetta**" on the forehead enables her to touch the words of the Fingers, incinerating her eyes. She relays them to the player and is then burned away by Frenzied Flame, leaving behind the Frenzied Flame Seal.
- If the player spares Melina and selects the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending, Melina's left eye unseals and she gains power over Destined Death, vowing to stop the player in a secret cutscene. If the player sacrifices Melina before meeting the Three Fingers, however, they shall melt away all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Lampreys** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The lampreys are eel-like humanoids distinguished by their eight eyes, circular jaws, and diminutive legs. They hunt using Glinting Nails and are the progenitors of the Finger Sorceries practiced by the finger-weavers. These enigmatic creatures can slip into white wormholes, enabling them to quickly teleport around the Finger Ruins they safeguard. Pearlescent Scales, a key component of Fingerprint Nostrum, grow inward deep within their skin. Some use this dubious form of esoteric medicine to transform their bodies into fingers, becoming lampreys instead.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.markdown:
Lampreys are either black or pale in appearance. All variants are gaunt, elongated figures with smooth, slippery skin. Dorsal and caudal fins line their long tails, which they use to prop themselves upright in a curved posture. Their drooped faces bear four sets of forward-facing, human-like eyes. They have five fingers on their large hands, but three digits on their vestigial feet. Strips of what appear to be shed skin or textile loosely cling to their lower body.

There are three variants of this enemy: Black Lamprey, White Lamprey, and Giant Lamprey.
Black Lamprey

The black lampreys are the standard variant of this enemy type.
White Lamprey
The pinkish-white lampreys dwell in the foggy Finger Ruins of Dheo. These individuals have additional attacks that deal Poison damage. They appear to vomit a mixture of blood, bile, and worms when fighting at short range.
Giant Lamprey
The largest lampreys are vigilant sentries that cast binding magic from afar. These creatures act as stationary turrets, maintaining their position and refusing to pursue distant targets that move out of their line of site. However, they are more active when fighting nearby targets.

Giant lampreys conjure explosive purple spheres and hurl them at their targets. Upon detonation, the blast stuns the victim with concentric purple rings for a few seconds. If their target is stunned by their Finger Snare attack, one nearby lamprey will teleport in to perform a grab attack.

sections.markdown: Merchant Kalé** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Kalé is a member of a tribe of Nomadic Merchants, scions of the Great Caravan who were spurned by Grace long ago. His ancestors were immured beneath the royal capital. Kalé is acquainted with Blaidd the Half-Wolf, considering him to be a good person despite being boorish.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Merchant Kalé is a nomadic merchant who has set up shop at the Church of Elleh in Limgrave, located north of the The First Step site of grace. He is the first merchant many players are likely to encounter, and is the only merchant who sells the Crafting Kit.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Internal name: **RedEyeGypsy**

sections.heading: Great Caravan
sections.markdown:
- Merchant Kalé had a full questline in which he actively searched for the lost Great Caravan. After acquiring the Burial Crow's Letter, his journey would have brought him to the Frenzied Flame Proscription, where he expressed tremendous anger toward the people of the Erdtree for what they did to his ancestors. Kalé then attempted to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame, but failed and was burned by the Three Fingers.
 - This questline may have been replaced or cut to avoid conflict with Lightseeker Hyetta's questline, as both arrived at the Frenzied Flame Proscription after directing the player to seek the Three Fingers.

sections.heading: Cursed Red Eyes
sections.markdown:
- In his earliest known draft, Kalé and the Nomadic Merchants were conceived as a single being divided into many bodies. They bore the cursed red eyes, an early version of the Frenzied Flame that threatened to blend them back together.
 - This version of Kalé and his brothers actively rode their mules and roamed the map, much like the Great Coffins pulled by Trolls.
 - The brothers were telepathically linked and dreamed together, but yearned to extinguish the flame and separate.
 - Kalé gave the player St. Trina's Crystal Ball, buying any collected Dream Mist, which staved off their curse.
 - St. Trina once becalmed the entombed Nomads with a lullaby, now played by Nomadic Merchants to calm themselves. Trina's cessation implies the Miquella-Trina abduction concept existed in early development.
 - In the final version of the game, Miquella's Needle serves as the means to quell the Frenzied Flame.
- Frenzied Flame melted away that which divided and distinguished at this stage of development.
- Killing Merchant Kalé or any of his brothers triggered Redeemer Guilbert to invade the player at several locations in Limgrave (then Tenebrae).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Melina** is a deuteragonist character in Elden Ring. She is a mysterious, spectral woman who offers an alliance with the Tarnished to help them on their journey to become Elden Lord. She may only be encountered when resting at specific Sites of Grace, though she may be summoned to help fight Morgott, the Omen King at the Elden Throne.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Melina has long observed the Lands Between. She was born at the foot of the Erdtree. She is a secret child of Queen Marika. Unlike Messmer or Morgott, Melina does not recall Marika with fondness.

At some point long ago, Melina bore a vision of fire. She was burned, leaving her bodiless; a drifting spirit bound to Grace.. Like her brother Messmer, she was assigned a purpose by Marika. However, she was unable to remember it. And so, Melina traveled with the spectral steed Torrent in search of the Tarnished who would lead her back to the foot of the Erdtree. There, she may ascertain her given purpose.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
Torrent identifies and selects a maidenless Tarnished, who recently washed up in the Stranded Graveyard, as one capable of brandishing the Elden Ring. Melina descends the spectral steed to grant the fallen champion a set of Sacred Flasks, choosing to aid them in violation of the Golden Order.

Sometime later, Melina approaches the Tarnished to offer them an accord: She could play the role of the missing Finger Maiden in return for a ride to the foot of the Erdtree. If the player desires the strength of runes, and, if they accept the accord, Melina entrusts them with the Spectral Steed Whistle and, therefore, Torrent. Melina advises them to follow the guidance of Grace and seek the shardbearer at Stormveil Castle.

Once the Tarnished defeats the demigod, Melina confesses that she was testing the Tarnished to see if they truly possessed the guidance of grace and if they were fit for the challenges to come. Satisfied with her new companion, Melina offers to take them to Roundtable Hold, a gathering place for Tarnished champions.

Throughout their journey, Melina also provides specks of guidance at certain sites of grace and, at churches dedicated to Queen Marika, she offers to reveal words spoken by Marika herself in the distant past.

sections.heading: Leyndell, Royal Capital
sections.markdown:
Upon arriving at their destination, the Royal Capital at the foot of the Erdtree, Melina thanks the Tarnished for escorting her and leaves to ascertain her purpose, claiming that she can govern her movement more freely there. She entrusts the power of runes and Torrent to the Tarnished. She will also offer her aid should the Tarnished challenge Morgott, the Omen King, ruler of Leyndell and guardian of the Erdtree.

After defeating Morgott, the Tarnished finds the path into the Erdtree barred by impenetrable thorns refusing entrance to all. Melina, having ascertained her purpose and seeing the Tarnished stuck, rejoins the Tarnished to say that she can burn the Erdtree to gain entrance inside, provided that she can get ahold of the Giants' Flame. And hence, she asks to go on a new journey, this time to the flame of ruin, far above the clouds, upon the snowy Mountaintops of the Giants. and tells them she will take care of the "kindling" required to set the tree alight.

Defeating Morgott also unseals a path to the Three Fingers. If the Tarnished rests at the nearest grace from their entombment, Melina will warn against meeting them and insist against inheriting the Frenzied Flame, for it would end all lives and births, which she cherishes. If the Tarnished heeds her warning, Melina and the protagonist will continue their journey for the flame of ruin.

sections.heading: Cardinal Sin
sections.markdown: When making their way to the Forge of the Giants, Melina clarifies that she is now acting of her own volition, regardless of the purpose that her mother gave her. After defeating the guardian of the flame, Melina puts her plan into action. She takes the Tarnished's hand, narcotizing them by doing so, and proceeds to sacrifice herself to channel the flame of ruin, setting the Erdtree aflame. The Tarnished, maidenless once more, wakes up at Crumbling Farum Azula. There, they must confront the Black Blade Maliketh and recover the Rune of Death. In this, Melina fulfills her purpose: *"The one who walks alongside flame, Shall one day meet the road of Destined Death."*

sections.heading: Destined Death
sections.markdown:
If the player ignores her warnings at the Frenzied Flame Proscription, or just inherits the Frenzied Flame without speaking with her, she will say that The Tarnished is no longer fit, ending her accord, and forever leaving their side but threatening to kill them should they become the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

If Melina did not fulfil her purpose as Kindling Maiden, an additional cutscene will play after the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending. At the Stone Platform, a chorus of whistling guides a transformed Melina to the Spectral Steed Whistle. She retrieves the smoldering ring from a pile of ash and holds it in her open palm. As Torrent's final remnants are consumed by the Frenzied Flame, Melina reveals her unsealed left eye and vows vengeance upon the player in the form of Destined Death.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.markdown:
Melina's questline runs parallel to the main story and is required to complete the game. It has two possible outcomes.
1. Stranded Graveyard
 - After fighting the Grafted Scion at the Chapel of Anticipation, Melina and Torrent appear during a cutscene. Melina grants the Flask of Crimson Tears and Flask of Cerulean Tears before departing.
1. Sites of Grace (Limgrave)
 - After leaving the Stranded Graveyard, activate and rest at either the Agheel Lake North or Gatefront Ruins Sites of Grace. A cutscene will play and Melina will offer an accord.
 - Alternatively, activate at any two Sites of Grace in the overworld and then rest at one of the following eight Sites of Grace: Agheel Lake North, Agheel Lake South, Bridge of Sacrifice, Church of Elleh, Gatefront Ruins, Seaside Ruins, Stormhill Shack, or Third Church of Marika.
 - *(Optional)* If you refuse her accord, you cannot enter Leyndell, Royal Capital, even with two Great Runes. You can reconsider at any time by selecting "Talk to Melina" at any Site of Grace.
 - Accepting grants the Spectral Steed Whistle, allowing you to summon Torrent.
1. *(Optional)* Sites of Grace
 - Melina may appear when you rest at any Site of Grace, offering the dialogue options "The Rays of Grace" and "Melina's Goal".
 - **Note**: these options will no longer be available once you progress to the next step.
 - Melina offers to share the words of Queen Marika when the player rests at one of the following Sites of Grace: Church of Pilgrimage, First Church of Marika, Grand Lift of Dectus, Minor Erdtree Church, Outer Wall Battleground, Queen's Bedchamber, and Third Church of Marika. Select "Talk to Melina" and accept to hear them.
1. Sites of Grace
 - Rest at any Site of Grace outside Limgrave or fight Margit, the Fell Omen at least once to trigger another conversation in which Melina extends an invitation to the Roundtable Hold. Accepting this invite is mandatory for accessing Leyndell, Royal Capital later in the game.
1. *(Optional)* Sites of Grace
 - After progressing Boc the Seamster's questline, Melina may appear to discuss him.
 - If Boc moves to the East Raya Lucaria Gate, Melina will appear there to ask about him.
 - If Boc moves to the Altus Highway Junction, Melina will appear there to ask about him again.
1. *(Optional)* Sites of Grace (Altus Plateau or Capital Outskirts)
 - Speak to Melina at any Site of Grace on the Altus Plateau or in the Capital Outskirts. This step is missed if the player enters Leyndell, Royal Capital.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital
 - Resting at a Site of Grace in Leyndell will trigger another interaction with Melina, after which she will leave you. Her dialogue options at various Sites of Grace will be temporarily unavailable.
 - Defeat Morgott, the Omen King.
 - *(Optional)* Melina may be summoned as a cooperator by activating her summon sign outside Morgott's boss room.
 - Approach the entrance to the Erdtree, turn back, and rest at the Elden Throne Site of Grace. Melina will appear and, after some dialogue, give you the Rold Medallion.
1. *(Ending A)* Mountaintops of the Giants
 - After defeating the Fire Giant and resting at the Forge of the Giants, you may talk to Melina. Speak to her and respond "I'm Ready" to commit the cardinal sin. Melina awakens the Giants' Flame, becomes its kindling, and burns the Erdtree. The player collapses and awakens in Crumbling Farum Azula.
 - **Note**: this ends Melina's questline, as her spirit . You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.
1. *(Ending B)* Frenzied Flame Proscription
 - Visit the Frenzied Flame Proscription and interact with the Three Fingers. Melina will appear at the next Site of Grace you rest at and will leave you permanently.
 - **Note**: this action cannot be reversed by using Celestial Dew at the Church of Vows or inserting Miquella's Needle at Dragonlord Placidusax. You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.
 - **Note**: you will gain the option "Listen to the flames" when resting at the Forge of the Giants Site of Grace, allowing progression to Crumbling Farum Azula. This unlocks an additional cutscene in the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Melina uses the Black Knife Assassin animation set.
- Attacks that produce lingering hazards can hit Melina when she sits at a Site of Grace, even applying Status Effects.
- Melina is a child of Marika and has access to her most secret incantation.
 - This incantation will also be automatically cast when she dies, even as a cooperator, the only way to see this in-game without modding.
- Melina can be summoned to help fight against Morgott.
 - Melina wields the Blade of Calling, which is golden flame counterpart to the Black Knife. Additionally, she uses two unplayable incantations that resemble the effects of Minor Erdtree and Miranda's Prayer.
- Melina is not a Finger Maiden.
- Melina is aware her agency will be restored if the Erdtree is destroyed.
- If the player spares Melina and chooses the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending, she will be transformed after Marika and the Erdtree are destroyed.
 - Melina's purpose remains the same, but its context becomes flipped: *"The one who walks alongside flame, Shall one day meet the road of Destined Death."*

sections.heading: Speculation
sections.markdown:
- It is implied that Melina is another child of Radagon and Marika:
 - **Naming Convention**: Most siblings in the Lands Between share the first letter of their name. Messmer/Melina/Miquella/Malenia would be no exception to this rule.
 - **Hair Color**: Melina's hair color seems to be a combination of Radagon and Marika's hair colors.
 - **Butterflies**: There are four butterfly items in-game, each representing a cursed demigod: Nascent Butterfly (Miquella), Aeonian Butterfly (Malenia), Black Pyrefly (Messmer), Smoldering Butterfly (Melina).
 - Messmer had a younger sister who also bore a vision of fire and, like Melina, he possessed the kindling to burn the Erdtree It is unknown when in the timeline Melina was born exactly, but she knew Marika's secret incantation and Messmer was the older brother of Radahn.
 - The soundtrack for Messmer's boss fight shares a leitmotif with Radagon's boss theme.
- Melina has an implied connection to the Gloam-Eyed Queen as she reveals her eye with a violet iris and inherits the power of Destined Death should the player spare her by using the Frenzied Flame as kindling.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Melina is internally named "**MaricaOfDaughter**" (ID: 2180).
- There are several lines of Melina's dialogue that can be heard in pre-launch game trailers that end up not being used in the main game. Whether they were envisioned as Melina's own words or spoken echoes of Queen Marika is not known.
 1. *The Tarnished will soon return ... guided by grace once lost.*
 1. *The Golden Order is broken to its core.*
 1. *They will fight. And they will die. In an unending curse.*
 1. *For how else is champion, or a lord, to be born?*
 1. *Brandish the Elden Ring ... for all of us.*

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Within the lands of Elden Ring are scattered various important elements the player should make themselves aware of.

sections.heading: Runes
sections.markdown: Runes can be obtained by defeating enemies or using items. Runes are used to level up your character's Stats and Attributes, buy items, and strengthen weapons and armor.

sections.heading: Site of Grace
sections.markdown:
There are rest points called Sites of Grace.

Resting at a Site of Grace will restore your HP, FP, and heal any status ailments. It will also refill all of your Sacred Flasks. Most of the enemies you have defeated will be revived when you rest at a Site of Grace.

sections.heading: How to use a Site of Grace
sections.markdown:
Approach the Site of Grace and press the [△/Y] button to activate it.
From here, pressing the [△/Y] button will bring up the menu and let you rest.
Sites of Grace that you have not reached yet emit rays of light.

sections.heading: Site of Grace menu
sections.markdown:
The Site of Grace menu is available while resting.
The selections available will change as the story progresses.
{| class="article-table"
|Pass Time||Move time forward in the game.
|-
|Level Up||Enhance your character’s stats.
|-
|Add Charge to Flask||Increase the number of times you can use the flask.
|-
|Increase Amount Replenished by Flasks||Enhance the flask’s restorative effect.
|-
|Distribute Flask Charges||Allocate the number of charges for your sacred flasks.
|-
| Memorize Spell||Equip magic you have learned in the memory slots to use it in the game. The number of slots available depends on your character’s status.
|-
|Mix Wondrous Physick||Mix acquired Crystal Tears to customize the effects of Flask of Wondrous Physick.
|-
|Sort Chest||Store items in or remove items from the chest.
|}

Sites of Grace that you already discovered will be saved on the map. Select the Site of Grace you want to travel to on the map, and you will move to that location. You cannot travel while in some dungeons.

sections.heading: Guidance of Grace
sections.markdown:
The light emanating from some Sites of Grace gives a hint as to where you may want to go next.

The Guidance of Grace can also be found in the map menu.

sections.heading: Summoning
sections.markdown:
When a rebirth monument is nearby and a monument icon is shown on the left side of the screen, you can use ashes to summon a spirit.

The summoned spirit will leave when its HP reaches zero, when a boss is defeated, when the spirit moves a certain distance away from the monument, or when the same ashes are used again.

Only one type of spirit can be summoned at a time, and spirits cannot be summoned during multiplayer.

sections.heading: Stakes of Marika
sections.markdown:
Upon dying, you will be revived at the last Site of Grace at which you rested. However, if you died near a Stake of Marika, you can choose to be revived there instead.

You can confirm if you are in the area of effect of a Stake of Marika by checking if the status icon (bow and arrow icon) appears.

sections.heading: Spectral Steed
sections.markdown:
Use the Spectral Steed Whistle to summon a Spectral Steed to ride.

If the Spectral Steed dies it can be summoned again, but it will consume a Flask of Crimson Tears.

sections.heading: Map
sections.markdown:
You can see your current location, terrain, buildings, and other information. Markers and landmarks can be placed on the map.

You can also go to a Site of Grace that you have discovered from the map menu.

You cannot open the map when you are engaged in battle.

sections.heading: Birdseye Telescope
sections.markdown: Use the Birdseye Telescopes in each area to see into the distance like a bird and get a better view of your destination.

sections.heading: Death
sections.markdown:
A character dies when their HP reaches zero.

When you die, all the runes you are carrying will be dropped. You can retrieve them by going back to the location of your death. If you die again before retrieving them, they will be lost.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Liurnian Civil War** was a event mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: A civil war between the Carian royal family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria broke out across Liurnia of the Lakes. It was the third and final major conflict in Liurnia, long after the First and Second Liurnian Wars with the people of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Prelude
sections.markdown:
After Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, was hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon left his wife Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon to become the second husband and King Consort of Queen Marika the Eternal. When Radagon departed and became second Elden Lord, Rennala's heart went with him, leaving her a grieving wreck. After Rennala's breakdown, the Academy realized that their queen did not have the unwavering strength of a true champion. With the Carian matriarch no longer in a state to oppose them, the Academy seized the opportunity to rebel against the Carian Royal Family and locked Rennala away in their Grand Library.

Rennala's weakened leadership was not the cause of the Academy's rebellion, merely the opportunity to do so. Their actual motive was a long-held resentment for the restriction of Primeval Current study enforced when Rennala became governor of the Academy. The Primeval Current is the origin of glintstone and the power behind all glintstone sorcey derived from the material. Exposing one's mind too deep into the Primeval Current's depths was a highly dangerous practice that had claimed the sanity of all sorcerers that did so. Rennala believed it was too risky and took steps to limit the practice during her appointment. However, the prevailing sentiment within the ambitious Academy did not agree. By overthrowing the Carians, they hoped to restore their once unabated research.

To aid in their insurrection, the Academy called upon their private army, the Knights of the Cuckoo. The Cuckoo were a group of mercenaries who had served a lucrative, longstanding contract defending the Academy's interests. Their symbol is a Cuckoo bird, its shrewd gaze representing their refusal to be mere servants of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. As part of their contract with the Academy, they were given free rein to wage war as they pleased, gaining an infamous reputation for their rapacious ways as a result. Another clause within their contract allowed them access to "faux sorceries", lesser, martial-focused, spells taught by the Academy. They loathed Albinaurics and found ways to weaponize their silver blood.

Meanwhile the Carians had long anticipated the Academy's eventual betrayal, and secretly prepared their forces for when the time would come. Firstly, they developed sorceries and battle arts that could absorb incoming spells, and reform their energy into glintblades to then be used against the caster. Secondly, the shields of the Carian Knights were specially made for defense against magical attacks.

sections.heading: Civil War
sections.markdown:
A major battle took place along the road north of the Liurnia Highway North Site of Grace, with the destroyed remains of Cuckoo Flame Chariots littering the roadside.

By some means, the Carian Knight, Moongrum, was able to take a defensive position at the lift that led to the Library, stopping any further harm coming to his queen.

sections.heading: The Siege of Caria Manor
sections.markdown:
The Siege of Caria Manor marked the end of the Cuckoos' offense into Caria. A magic snare resulted in a total Carian victory. Captured Cuckoos consumed Seluvis's Potion, and were enthralled as living puppets.

The Cuckoos withdrew, but the Carians never recovered. Though Ranni the Witch returned to the Manor following the conflict, her house was already ousted.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Man-Flies** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Man-Flies are insectoid humans, blindfolded and wrapped in soiled linens. These gregarious creatures thrive among filth, commonly inhabiting the squalid cisterns and sewers of the Realm of Shadow. Their backs bear large, veined insect wings while their lower bodies have transformed into elongated abdomens, protected by a hardened tergum. They often crawl on all six limbs, but can hover just above the ground by buzzing their translucent wings.

Man-Flies deal Standard damage and are weakest to Fire damage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Man-flies were once hornsent who were afflicted with the dreadful fly sickness. Many sick were tossed from the wooden platform at the Abandoned Ailing Village into the depths. Their bodies have accumulated into a large mound in the Ellac River down below. It is said they were freed from their suffering as the metamorphosis took hold, and that those who cared for them were unaffected.

A hornsent moldmonger cultivated the flesh and blood of man-flies into a Fly Mold that could be used for making Jar Dwellers.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.markdown:
There are two variants of the Man-Fly:
- Man-Fly
- Man-Fly Spitter

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Man-Flies at Belurat, Tower Settlement are immune to Poison ailment buildup.
- Man-Flies cannot attack while in flight.
- Man-Fly Spitters lack melee attacks.
- Man-Fly Ashes is a Spirit Ash that summons two Man-Flies and one Man-Fly Spitter.
- Man-Flies shed their exoskeletons as they grow larger. Many of these discarded shells litter areas where Man-Flies are common.
 - Large shed exoskeletons can be found but no Man-Fly in the game is big enough to have left them.
- The Ailment Talisman is found at the Abandoned Ailing Village on the wooden platform from which bodies were dumped.
- A Man-Fly in a shack at the Abandoned Ailing Village prays to a pile of corpses containing the [[item:greater-potentate-s-cookbook-10|Greater Potentate's Cookbook [10]]], which unlocks Hefty Fly Pot.
- Shadow Undead at the Abandoned Ailing Village cast Swarm of Flies, an incantation associated with the Formless Mother.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Liurnian Wars** were a series of events mentioned in Elden Ring. There were two wars between Caria and the Academy and the Golden Order, culminating in the marriage of Rennala and Radagon.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: After the end of the Erdtree's Age of Plenty, the Carian royal family and their allies at the Academy of Raya Lucaria anticipated conflict with the Erdtree. The Carian Knights thus steeled themselves for eventual battle against Marika's holy golden forces.

sections.heading: First Liurnian War
sections.markdown: A mighty champion with flowing red locks, Radagon of the Golden Order joined the heroes' ranks when he invaded Liurnia at the head of a great golden host, and clashed against the enchanted forces of the Rennala, the Full Moon Witch. Although the Grace of Gold empowered his forces, the Knights of Caria were their equal match. Although both sides achieved glory, the war ended inconclusively; neither emerged as the victor.

sections.heading: Second Liurnian War
sections.markdown: Radagon returned to do battle with Rennala once more and was again evenly matched. He eventually repented his territorial aggressions by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew, and swore his love to Rennala. He became the husband of the Carian Queen, wedding her at the Church of Vows. Rennala bequeathed him a greatsword, bestowed by a Carian queen upon her spouse to honor long-standing tradition.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.markdown:
- Peace between Altus and Liurnia. Marriage between Rennala, Queen of Liurnia, and Radagon, Prince of the Erdtree. Houses of the Moon and the Erdtree conjoined.
- Liurnia assimilated into the Golden Order. Radagon accesses Raya Lucaria's knowledge.
- After joining the Carian line, he ordered the Carian magic preceptors to don masks of confidence, to make it clear that all of their matters were to be kept strictly private.
